To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity-dependent fos gene is expressed in layer 2 pyramids that are targeted by axon terminals from the posteromedian nucleus, a thalamic nucleus that is associated with broad receptive field and widespread cortical projections.
the expression of fosGFP in the mouse barrel cortex is a reliable marker of POm-targeted, multi-whisker responsive neurons.
a subset of cortical layer 2 pyramids, distinguished by expression from the fosGFP reporter, are targeted by POm axons and are preferentially activated by stimulation of surround whiskers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the somatosensory system in the mouse.
the mechanisms underlying sensory perception and behavior in the mouse somatosensory system.
how sensory experience shapes cortical circuits and how this information is encoded.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fosGFP-expressor neurons in the juvenile somatosensory barrel cortex receive input from POm, which is consistent with the known physiology of these thalamic nuclei.

the activity-dependent fos GFP reporter gene labels a subset of layer two pyramidal neurons in the juvenile mouse whisker somatosenosry cortex that are preferentially activated by stimulation of the surround whisker field.
fosGFP(+) excitatory neurons are not specifically activated by whisker deflection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fosGFP-exhibiting neurons in the barrel cortex are preferentially targeted by POm, and are more likely to be activated by multi-whisker stimuli.

a subpopulation of layer 2 pyramids in mouse somatosensory neocortex, which express fosGFP in response to whisker stimulation, have receptive field properties that are consistent with their targeting by axons from POm, a nucleus that has been associated with the processing of multi-whisker information in the whisker somatosensor cortex.
the fosGFP reporter labels neurons that are targeted by POm, and that these neurons have a broad receptive field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a subset of excitatory cortical neurons are preferentially targeted by thalamocortical afferents with broad receptive fields.
the fosGFP reporter can be used to identify a subset of cortical layer 2 pyramids that are targeted by POm axons.
the fosGFP expression pattern is not a good indicator of the receptive field properties of cortical neurons.
